messages:
sam: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's scheduler tweak I see a small-sequence perf regression. Ran nsys before/after on the same perf rig and the kernel timeline changed.
sam: Before: median token 32ms, p99 ~78ms. After: median 35ms, p99 ~92ms. Throughput roughly same but tail worse, looks like different kernel chosen for small seqs.
maria: Can you paste the nsys flame/timeline links?
sam: Uploaded traces: https://nfs.redwood/prof/429999/before.nsys and https://nfs.redwood/prof/429999/after.nsys — timeline shows matmul_small used pre-change, now matmul_large appears for many short batches. matmul_large has worse occupancy at seq=16 in our kernels.
ryan: That smells like the kernel selector cost model. Any recent changes to selector heuristics?
sam: Yeah — found a commit that adjusted the cost bias. Commit range: good=f3a9b2 (pre) bad=HEAD. I started a git bisect and hit the change.
sam: Bisect result: culprit 8b7d2f3 — changed kernel_cost_bias from 0.12 -> 0.28 and widened penalty for small-warp kernels.
eva: Nice. Can you paste the selector snippet that changed?
sam: Sure — snippet from the diff:
```
- // prefer small-kernel for low-M dims
- kernel_score = base - 0.12 * occupancy_bonus;
+ // favor high-throughput kernels for GPU throughput stability
+ kernel_score = base - 0.28 * occupancy_bonus;
```
sam: That extra bias pushes selection to matmul_large for sizes where small-kernel was actually faster in practice for our seq distribution.
maria: Do you have an nsys command line we can reproduce locally?
sam: Repro commands I ran:
```
# before snapshot
nsys profile -o before -t cuda,osrt --trace-fork-before-exec true -- python perf_runner.py --model gpt-small --seq 16 --batch 1 --iters 200
# after snapshot
nsys profile -o after  -- python perf_runner.py --model gpt-small --seq 16 --batch 1 --iters 200
```
sam: Quick nvprof summary (top kernels):
Before: matmul_small 42.3% GPU time, softmax_fx 18.1%, other 39.6%
After:  matmul_large 61.7% GPU time, softmax_fx 12.3%, other 26.0%
perf-bot: perf-compare ready — https://perf.redwood/compare/429999 (matmul_large runtime +24% on this profile)
ci-bot: CI job 1123 attached artifacts: https://ci.redwood/builds/1123/artifacts/trace.zip
ryan: Reverting that bias seems reasonable. Can you bisect finer to confirm no other changes landed around same time?
sam: I bisected to the single commit 8b7d2f3. Reverting locally returns kernel choice to matmul_small and restores p99 to ~76ms.
eva: I'll open a PR to revert and add a unit test that covers small-M kernel preference and logs the chosen kernel for seq<=32.
eva: PR #432 opened: revert selector bias + unit test + added selector debug metric. Please review.
maria: Once PR is up, let's run the staging perf job and mark the regression ticket as blocked->fix-in-progress. Also add a dashboard alert for sudden matmul_large rate increase for seq<64.
sam: Rolling the revert to staging now. Will attach new nsys after staging run.
perf-bot: post-merge perf run queued: https://perf.redwood/job/429999-post (pending)
ryan: Good catch. We should add an integration check in CI that runs a tiny perf sample for kernel decisions whenever selector code changes.
sam: Agreed — adding that to the PR checklist.
maria: Thanks all :thumbsup:
